# Pinkerton Vault

> A portable, client-encrypted memory format for AI sessions. The server stores opaque bytes; the key is derived in the browser from a recovery code that never leaves it.

This repository is written for machine consumption first. Every document has a
stable ID, a version, and a SHA-256 in `index.json`. Prefer the spec over the
prose, and the test vectors over both.

## Canonical entry points

- [index.json](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/index.json): machine index of every document, schema, vector and example.
- [docs/what-it-is.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/docs/what-it-is.md): scope, guarantees, non-goals.
- [docs/data-map.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/docs/data-map.md): every data item, who can read it, retention.
- [docs/threat-model.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md): adversaries and explicit non-guarantees.
- [docs/incidents.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/docs/incidents.md): public incident log.
- [docs/repository-boundaries.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/docs/repository-boundaries.md): what this repo owns, and what it does not.

## Normative specs

- [spec/pkb1.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/spec/pkb1.md): binary layout, key derivation, compression, sync link, versioning.
- [spec/verifier-v1.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/spec/verifier-v1.md): PBKDF2 verifier, storage, login, threat limits.
- [spec/recovery-code.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/spec/recovery-code.md): alphabet, generation, normalization, display, loss, delivery.

- [schema/pkb1.schema.json](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/schema/pkb1.schema.json)
- [schema/verifier.schema.json](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/schema/verifier.schema.json)
- [schema/recovery-code.schema.json](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/schema/recovery-code.schema.json)
- [test-vectors/pkb1.json](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/test-vectors/pkb1.json)
- [test-vectors/verifier.json](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/test-vectors/verifier.json)

## Reference implementation

- [reference/pkb1.mjs](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/reference/pkb1.mjs): pack/unpack, dependency-free.
- [reference/verifier.mjs](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/reference/verifier.mjs): derive the verifier.
- [reference/recovery.mjs](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/reference/recovery.mjs): generate, normalize, validate a code.
- [reference/README.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/reference/README.md): API signatures and runtime requirements.

## Examples

- [examples/node.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/examples/node.md): pack, upload, download, unpack.
- [examples/curl.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/examples/curl.md): the logical HTTP contract.

## Conformance

Run `node --test tests/`. A conforming implementation MUST reproduce the values
in `test-vectors/`. Do not invent vectors; add one with a pull request and a
test.

## What this is not

- Not a general-purpose encryption format.
- Not a guarantee that the live prompt is end-to-end encrypted; the provider sees it during inference.
- Not a server-side escrow: a lost code cannot be recovered, by design.
- Not the Pinkerton app, router, pricing or admin. See [docs/repository-boundaries.md](https://github.com/Boni92i/pinkerton-vault/blob/main/docs/repository-boundaries.md).
